name: KeeLoq HCS remote (rolling code, identification only)
description: Microchip HCS encoder (HCS200/300/301 and clones) used in gate, garage and alarm remotes. A preamble of about twelve 1:1 pulses, a header gap of ten elements, then 66 bits sent least significant first: '1' is one element of carrier and two of silence, '0' two and one. Bits 0-31 are the encrypted hopping code, which changes on every press; bits 32-59 the serial number, 60-63 the buttons, 64 low battery and 65 repeat. Fields are numbered in the frame as this definition stores it, most significant first after the least-significant-first transmission is reversed. This definition only recognises the frame and splits it into those parts: the hopping code is shown as received and is never decrypted. The element is set by the encoder's oscillator, hence the range. Draft because the structure was confirmed on a private recording that, being a rolling code, may not be distributed.
